findings.title: Team admin/owner check is AND, so it never matches
findings.body: Permission is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), but those membership roles are alternatives (the flag is even named isTeamAdminOrOwner, and the bookings UI uses isUserTeamAdminOrOwner). If the roles are mutually exclusive the expression is always false, because a failed admin check short-circuits and a successful admin check then fails the owner check. A team admin or owner who is not the booking host and whose login email is not already an attendee is always rejected with FORBIDDEN, so they cannot add guests to team bookings from the bookings page.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees is invoked through an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking query already loads booking.user.credentials and the host destination calendar, but those credentials are never used. Anyone allowed by the attendee check (and any team manager, once the role check is fixed) will try to patch the host's calendar event with their own OAuth tokens. That call fails or updates the wrong account, so the new guests never land on the host calendar. The attendee rows are already committed by then, and a retry treats those emails as duplicates and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update cannot be completed.

findings.title: Guests are committed before calendar and email side effects
findings.body: prisma.booking.update createMany inserts attendees immediately, with no transaction around the later calendar update and sendAddGuestsEmails. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the tRPC mutation fails but the rows stay. The client shows an error, yet a retry filters those addresses out as already attending and, when no other new addresses remain, returns BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid. The guests exist in the database, the host calendar is unchanged, and no notification is sent, with no way to finish the operation for those addresses.

findings.title: Seated events are not enforced and hidden attendees are emailed
findings.body: seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees are copied onto the calendar event and then ignored. The handler still createMany's Attendee rows with no BookingSeat / seat-reference rows and no capacity check. On a seated event that overbooks the slot, leaves people who do not show up in seat cancellation or no-show flows, and skips per-seat payment. sendAddGuestsEmails then sends AttendeeScheduledEmail with the full attendee list. Unlike sendScheduledSeatsEmails, it never passes showAttendees, so an event type with seatsShowAttendees false leaks every other attendee's name and email to the newly added addresses.

findings.title: Guest filter misses blacklist, case, and in-request duplicates
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but each submitted guest is tested with includes(guest) and compared to existing attendees with guest === attendee.email, with no toLowerCase or trim. Zod's email check allows mixed case, so Spam@blocked.com bypasses a blacklist entry of spam@blocked.com, and A@x.com is inserted even when a@x.com is already an attendee. The variable is named uniqueGuests but the filter never dedupes the input, and the schema does not either, so one request can create two Attendee rows for the same address. There is also no unique (bookingId, email) guard around the check-then-insert, so two concurrent calls can both pass the read and insert the same guest twice.

findings.title: Cancelled, pending, past, and no-guest event types are accepted
findings.body: After the booking is loaded, nothing checks BookingStatus, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests. A direct call can add attendees to a cancelled, rejected, or still-pending booking and sendAddGuestsEmails will mail ICS REQUEST invites marked CONFIRMED, including the video URL and meeting password when a video reference exists. The same path ignores disableGuests, so an event type that turned guests off still accepts invites. Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee is authorized, not only the host, so a booker can do this even when the host disabled guests. The bookings UI also offers the action for past confirmed rows, because Add guests lives on bookedActions and that menu is rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem.

findings.title: Emails are selected from the raw guest list, not guests actually added
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, every current attendee whose email is in that array receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new booking confirmation plus ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Submitting an address that was already on the booking therefore sends that person a fresh 'you are scheduled' invite, which calendar clients treat as a new or duplicate event. Addresses that were filtered out as duplicates still match and take the wrong template; only the addresses that were actually inserted should get the scheduled email.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails
findings.body: Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before mailing. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take eventTypeMetadata and always emails the organizer, every attendee, and each new guest. The handler loads eventType but never forwards metadata.disableStandardEmails. Event types that turned standard host or attendee emails off still get a full fan-out, including video-call details, whenever someone uses this mutation.

findings.title: Guest list has no maximum, so one call can mass-mail
findings.body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() and no uniqueness constraint, and addGuests is a plain authedProcedure rather than the bookings procedure used by editLocation. A host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation. Each new address becomes an Attendee row and receives AttendeeScheduledEmail with the meeting link and, when present, the video meeting password. That is an authenticated email-spam and meeting-link disclosure path with no cap.

findings.title: Email failures are swallowed and reported as success
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch that only console.log's a static string and drops err. The handler then returns { message: 'Guests added' }, and the dialog shows the success toast and closes. If the mailer throws, guests are stored and the calendar may already have been updated, but nobody is notified and the user is told the operation succeeded. The log line does not include the error, so the failure is also invisible in production logs.

findings.title: Collective/round-robin hosts are never notified or updated
findings.body: The CalendarEvent built for this flow never sets team (or the other hosts' destination calendars). sendAddGuestsEmails only loops calendarEvent.team.members, so that loop is dead and co-hosts do not get OrganizerAddGuestsEmail. destinationCalendar is only the booking calendar or the single booking.user calendar. On collective or round-robin events, other hosts keep a stale attendee list on their calendars and receive no email that guests were added.

findings.title: New guests are stored with an empty name
findings.body: Every added guest is inserted with name: ''. Attendee emails address them as ' <email>' (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail / AttendeeScheduledEmail use `${name} <${email}>`), and the ICS ATTENDEE CN is blank. Some clients drop or mis-file invites with an empty CN, and the organizer subject uses attendees[0].name, which is an empty string when that row is first. The email local-part or the address itself should be stored as the name, which is what booking-time guests already do.

findings.title: No tests for auth, seat rules, or email recipient selection
findings.body: The new mutation changes booking attendees, calendar events, and a multi-recipient email fan-out, and the PR adds no handler or email tests. Nothing covers the admin-versus-owner permission expression, blacklist and case-folding, rejection of seated or disableGuests event types, cancelled or past bookings, or which template is sent to new versus existing attendees. Those branches are where the implementation is wrong, and they will not be caught by typecheck.
